sections.title: AWS for a backend developer

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: Your Git, Docker and CI/CD guide (Part 4) already covers cloud foundations, IAM and running a service on ECS. This page adds the map of services you will be asked about. You do not need all of AWS: learn these, and what each is for.

rows: Object storage; not a file system
Load balancer, API front door, CDN

sections.title: Three ideas that come up constantly
blocks: **Shared responsibility.** AWS secures the cloud; you secure what you put in it: IAM, open ports, encryption settings and your code.
**IAM roles, not keys.** A service gets temporary credentials through a role. Long-lived access keys in code or configuration are the classic leak. Grant the least privilege needed.

**Regions and Availability Zones.** A region holds several isolated AZs. Run across at least two AZs for availability; go multi-region only when the business truly needs it, because it is far more complex.

blocks.title: AWS SDK for Java v2
Gotcha: surprise bills
blocks.text: Set a budget alarm before you create anything. NAT gateways, idle RDS instances, and data transfer are common surprises when practising.

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: **ECS or EKS?** ECS with Fargate is simpler and enough for most teams. EKS makes sense when you need Kubernetes' portability and ecosystem, or already have the skills, because it costs more to operate.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Learn the service map, not all of AWS.
- Use IAM roles and least privilege; no long-lived keys.
- Run across two or more Availability Zones.
- Set a budget alarm first.

items.question: SQS or SNS?
items.answer: SQS is a queue that one group of workers consumes. SNS pushes to many subscribers. They are often combined: SNS fans out to several SQS queues.

items.question: Why is S3 a poor place for frequently edited files?
items.answer: Objects are replaced whole, with no partial update or file locking. It suits immutable objects served at scale.
